spec.name: addcarry-rot-xor-v1
spec.limitations: Still per-byte with an 8-bit key: no cross-byte diffusion (equal plaintext bytes give equal ciphertext bytes at every offset) and a single known plaintext/ciphertext byte pair narrows the key to a 256-candidate scan, so it fails immediately under known-plaintext or repeated-structure analysis. The added add_key step also means the inverse's final move is a secret-dependent modular subtraction (add 256-k) that the fixed op set cannot express, so decryption needs a host-side 256-k computation; the construction is exactly invertible, but its inverse is not a program in this instruction set. Using the key twice adds no entropy beyond the 256 possible keys and no extra secret state.
spec.math: With k the secret byte: x1 = x + k (mod 256), x2 = rol1(x1), x3 = x2 xor 90, x4 = rol2(x3), x5 = x4 + 201 (mod 256), x6 = x5 xor k, y = rol7(x6). Each step is a bijection on the 256-byte set: xor with a constant is an involution, addition mod 256 is a permutation with inverse add(256-c), and rol n permutes the 8 bit positions with inverse rol((8-n) mod 8), so rol1/rol7 and rol2/rol6 are inverse pairs. A composition of bijections is a bijection, hence exactly invertible for every k. Inversion runs reversed ops with reversed arguments: y -> rol 1 -> xor k -> add 55 (= -201) -> rol 6 -> xor 90 -> rol 7 -> add (256-k), recovering x; only that last subtraction lies outside the op set.
spec.assumptions: The key k is a fixed secret byte chosen uniformly and reused for every input byte; ops apply independently per byte with rol wrapping inside 8 bits (n reduced mod 8); all other operands are public constants; decryption is performed by a host that can compute 256-k; no nonce, IV, or chaining is assumed; *_key operands are ignored.
